settings.title: Whenever we use the words ‘cult’, ‘cultism’ or ‘cultist’ we are referring solely to the phenomenon where troubling levels of undue psychological influence may exist. This phenomenon can occur in almost any group or organisation.

settings.editor: Dialogue Ireland, Services We Offer

settings.title: Where would you like to start?

settings.description_text: Worried about a group, a relationship or a belief, yours or someone else’s? Start here.
Plain-language guides, our mission, the history of Dialogue Ireland and the Schools’ Programme.
2,800+ articles on hundreds of groups, A–Z. Briefing documents, media from 1974, conferences and books.
An independent trust and registered charity. Who we are, what we do, how to support the work.

settings.editor: Whichever of these sounds like you, you are welcome here. You do not need to be sure of anything.

settings.title: I’m in a group and I have doubts

settings.editor: Having doubts is not disloyalty, and it does not mean something is wrong with you. You do not have to decide anything today. You can ask questions and take your time.

Leaving can bring relief, grief, anger and confusion, sometimes in the same hour. These reactions are common. We can listen, help you make sense of what happened and point you to people who understand.
It is hard to watch someone you love change. Staying in contact and staying calm usually matters more than winning an argument. Write to us and we can talk through your situation.
Teachers, clergy, counsellors, journalists and officials can ask us for information and for referral. We also run a Schools’ Programme.
A few lines are enough. You do not need to name the group.
We help clarify whether the concern is about cultism or about something else.
Where another kind of help fits, we refer you to people who understand.
If someone is in immediate danger, call 112 or 999. Some people come back to us after months or even two years. That is fine.
Draft copy for review by Dialogue Ireland. Help section written by Svetlana Krylova.
